scope: Generic diagram resources; deployment/service identity must disambiguate self-hosted from managed behavior before implementation.

resources.currentImplementation: Entry point injects application RPS; fallback 5000, generic CPU/memory, fixed cost and common faults.
resources.realityGap: No name/query, answer, TTL, resolver cache, negative cache, timeout or authoritative/recursive role. HTTP routing is not DNS resolution.
resources.targetBehavior: Explicit resolver/authoritative identity, query class, TTL/cache state, name-to-endpoint dependencies and bounded query service. Managed-service CPU/memory/storage and replica scaling remain opaque/not applicable unless a self-hosted server is selected; expose queries, cache outcomes, resolution failures and priced query usage.

resources.currentImplementation: Generic pass-through, capacity 20000 RPS and bandwidth proxy, no edge cache behavior.
resources.realityGap: No object identity, cache policy, origin traffic, expiry, geography or invalidation.
resources.targetBehavior: Request/cacheability classes, byte/working-set cache state, TTL/eviction and origin miss work; link reachability and transfer metering. Provider limits/cost by service and geography. Internal provider CPU and physical replicas are opaque; no invented percentages or scaling controls.

resources.currentImplementation: Entry/pass-through resource with fallback capacity; public/encryption/open-port flags are static warnings.
resources.realityGap: No rule evaluation, denied work, state table, listener or protocol semantics. Diagram presence gives no protection.
resources.targetBehavior: Explicit L3/L4/L7 service identity, policy/reachability and allowed/denied flow counters, connection state where applicable. Appliance capacity from configured demand; managed internals opaque. Storage/scaling only for a selected appliance implementation, never implied by the icon.

resources.currentImplementation: Equal VM split, pools, previous-tick shedding logs, CPU autoscaling policy and pending replicas.
resources.realityGap: No real connection/request limits, queues, health probes, affinity, detection lag or response routing.
resources.targetBehavior: Composable routing policy, endpoint eligibility, connection/pending-request limits and backpressure, probe/detection events, byte/link work. Keep pool control distinct from LB service. M2A proves only deterministic sorted round robin; other mechanisms and LB consumption are pending.

resources.currentImplementation: SKU vCPU/baseline multiplied by80, write tax, synthetic memory/connections, pool and vertical restart state.
resources.realityGap: Host capability is conflated with application throughput; no CPU credits, scheduler, memory allocations, worker queue, sockets or app readiness.
resources.targetBehavior: Host capability plus separate application service-demand profile; bounded workers/queues, CPU-time and memory allocations, connection pools and deadlines. Provision/readiness/drain events and stateful credits later. M2A uses explicitly reserved CPU shares and synchronous dependency slots, not a full CPU scheduler.

resources.currentImplementation: Generic serving resource with1000 RPS, no artifact lifecycle.
resources.realityGap: Registry traffic should arise from push/pull/startup work, not every application request.
resources.targetBehavior: Image manifests/layers, cache reuse, authentication/reachability, byte transfer, storage and operation quotas; deployment startup creates pull work and readiness delay. Managed CPU/replica scaling opaque; self-hosted implementation can compose compute/storage queues. Expose pull bytes, failures and startup blocking.

resources.currentImplementation: Global80% hit ratio, recomputed global RPS and memory formula; failed cache forwards all read demand.
resources.realityGap: No cache contents, TTL, invalidation, eviction, warm-up or persistent state. No measured misses/hits.
resources.targetBehavior: Small explicit key/object or calibrated reuse-distance model; bytes/working set, TTL, capacity, eviction and cold start. Misses generate dependency work; connection/CPU queues consume service demand. Persistence/storage I/O only when configured; crash loss and warm-up differ from fault expiry.

resources.currentImplementation: QPS/vCPU125, global workload factor, VMs×20 connections, limit pressure forces CPU≥95, vertical restart.
resources.realityGap: No pool lifecycle, actual queries, query working memory, I/O, lock waits, transactions, consistency or recovery state.
resources.targetBehavior: Query-class CPU/memory/I/O demand, client pool and server reserved connection limits, queue/admission and contention domains. Buffer cache, writes/WAL/checkpoints, replicas/failover require separate calibration. M2A proves only bounded active connection/service slots with serial CPU/I/O and blocked callers; it is not PostgreSQL emulation.

resources.currentImplementation: Generic2000 RPS and bandwidth proxy, no stored objects/bytes or operation outcomes.
resources.realityGap: No PUT/GET/LIST/delete classes, size/prefix distribution, quotas, durability or storage billing.
resources.targetBehavior: Operation/byte work, object inventory, partitioned quotas, request/transfer/storage metering, authorization/reachability and retryable errors. Managed internal CPU/memory/physical disk failure and replica scaling are opaque; never infer data loss from endpoint unavailability.

resources.currentImplementation: Generic5000 RPS pass-through; no message backlog.
resources.realityGap: A queue icon has no producer/consumer/acknowledgement, retention or redelivery mechanism.
resources.targetBehavior: Messages with identity/bytes, publish acceptance, ready/unacked backlog, consumers and prefetch/concurrency, acknowledgement, visibility/expiry, retry budgets and DLQ. Persistence and replication are configured durability mechanisms. Backlog and work conservation drive pressure/recovery and operation/storage cost.

resources.currentImplementation: Fixed CPU12/memory18 and generic cost; diagram edges do not create a telemetry pipeline.
resources.realityGap: No scrape/export interval, sample bytes/cardinality, local buffer, telemetry loss or target overhead.
resources.targetBehavior: Configured collection/export work, target sampling overhead, finite buffers, loss/backpressure and exporter reachability. Local memory/CPU/storage measured only from explicit demand/allocation. Replica autoscaling is not an agent behavior; host deployment count belongs to the orchestrator. Agent failure must not make application availability fail automatically.
